1	# Mission Control MVP v0
2	
3	## Background
4	The customer is the operations team of an organization (org). An org can be a space agency or a private company.
5	
6	Mission leads spend hours to cross-reference skill profiles, availability calendars and existing commitments. Mission staffing is the bottleneck. Mission Control finds qualified and available crew members for a mission and makes sure that they are not overloaded.
7	
8	| User | Responsibility |
9	|------|----------------|
10	| Mission lead (power user) | Manages missions. Staffs them with qualified and available crew members. |
11	| Director | Approves or rejects missions. Oversees the org. Manages org settings (skills). |
12	| Crew member | Manages their profile (skills and availability). Accepts or declines assignments. |
13	
14	## Requirements
15	### P0
16	P0 is the first version that is ready to pitch to a customer.
17	
18	**Delivery**
19	1. A reviewer clones the GitHub repository and runs it locally in minutes. The repository contains setup instructions, demo seed data, this design document, the API and the CLI.
20	2. The repository contains evidence of verification: test output and a scripted CLI demo.
21	3. The seed data has 2 orgs and 2 directors in one org. It has enough crew members to show the matcher trade-offs: experts against closest fit, leave and workload.
22	
23	**Auth and tenant**
24	
25	4. Each org is a separate tenant with exclusive data access. The data-access layer and composite foreign keys enforce this.
26	5. Each user has one role: director, lead or crew member. The API enforces the role permissions.
27	6. A user logs in to the CLI as a seeded user (`mc login --user username`).
28	7. For a forbidden action, the CLI shows a clear error with the role and the rule.
29	
30	**Mission lifecycle**
31	
32	8. Each mission needs approval. The lead submits the mission to a director.
33	9. The director approves or rejects the mission. The approval view shows the matcher preview.
34	10. Crew members accept or decline assignments.
35	11. Directors see the whole org: all missions and all crew members (API and CLI).
36	
37	**Crew and skills**
38	
39	12. Crew members manage their skill profile via the CLI. They list, add, update and remove their own skills from the org catalogue, with a proficiency level.
40	13. Crew members manage their availability via the CLI. They list, add and remove their own unavailability.
41	14. Crew members see their own assignments with history (past, declined), their profile and the mission details. They accept or decline assignments.
42	15. Each org has its own set of skills. P0 seeds the skills. P1 adds skill editing.
43	
44	**Matching**
45	
46	16. The matcher suggests crew members for a mission. The inputs are skills, availability and workload.
47	17. The lead runs a read-only matcher preview in DRAFT to check that the mission can be staffed.
48	18. The lead invites crew members only when the mission is APPROVED.
49	19. Rematching fills only open slots. It never suggests a crew member who declined this mission.
50	
51	**CLI**
52	
53	20. The primary workflows run through the CLI. See [CLI](#cli).
54	
55	**Quality**
56	
57	21. Tests cover the happy path per workflow: lifecycle, matcher, invites and responses, crew profile.
58	22. Cross-org access checks make sure that resources of another org return 404.
59	23. A scripted end-to-end CLI demo runs the full mission lifecycle over the seed data.
60	
61	#### Build order
62	Each step ends with its happy path test and its cross-org check. Each step is one or more commits.
63	
64	1. Skeleton: docker-compose Postgres, FastAPI app, Alembic, Typer entry point, README run steps.
65	2. Data model, first migration and seed data: 2 orgs, 2 directors in one org, leads, crew, skills, leave, existing assignments for workload.
66	3. Auth and tenant: `mc login`, JWT with `user_id`, per-request load of user, org and role, org-scoped data-access layer, RBAC error format.
67	4. Missions in DRAFT: create, edit, slots, list, show.
68	5. Matcher preview: filters, ranking, slot assignment. `mc missions match`.
69	6. Approval: submit, withdraw, approve, reject. No self approval, additional director flag, matcher preview in the approval view.
70	7. Staffing: invite, `mc assignments list / accept / decline`, double booking check, decliner exclusion on rematch.
71	8. Remaining transitions: withdraw from APPROVED to DRAFT, start (with guard), complete, cancel. Assignment cancellation.
72	9. Crew profile: `mc profile show`, skills, availability.
73	10. Org crew view: directors and leads list and show the crew members of the org (requirement 11). Leads see leave as "unavailable" without the reason.
74	11. Scripted end-to-end CLI demo and test results in the README.
75	
76	### P1
77	P1 extends the MVP if time permits in this session.
78	
79	1. Directors manage the org skill catalogue.
80	2. Mission audit logs.
81	3. Decision insights for the lead: why the matcher excluded a crew member.
82	4. Rank breakdown per suggestion: why a crew member is the best fit for the slot.
83	5. Short references for missions (`MSN-<n>`) and skills (`slug`) in the CLI. See [Short references](#short-references).
84	
85	### P2
86	P2 is out of scope for this session.
87	
88	| Area | Item |
89	|------|------|
90	| Auth and tenant | Noisy-neighbour protection and uneven org sizes |
91	| | Real IdP (OIDC), login and signup |
92	| | Postgres RLS as a second layer for reads |
93	| | User and role management |
94	| Mission lifecycle | Approval workflow customization |
95	| | Crew members withdraw after they accept |
96	| | Reject with comment, cancel with reason |
97	| | Reassign the lead of a mission |
98	| Crew and skills | Edit and archive skills |
99	| | Verification of self-assessed proficiency |
100	| Matching | Additional resource constraints |
101	| | Report of skill gaps and possible resolutions when no match exists |
102	| | Rest buffer between missions |
103	| | Mission priority |
104	| | Optimization for large orgs |
105	| Operations | CI/CD |
106	| | Scalability, observability, IaC, offline jobs |
107	
108	## Tech stack
109	The API and the CLI use one language (Python). This keeps the stack small.
110	
111	| Component | Choice | Reason |
112	|-----------|--------|--------|
113	| CLI | Typer, httpx, Rich | Typed commands, generated help, readable tables. The CLI calls the API and stores the token locally after login. |
114	| API | FastAPI, Pydantic | Typed API with generated OpenAPI docs. |
115	| Data access | SQLAlchemy, Alembic | Safe DB access with migrations. |
116	| Database | Postgres | |
117	| Auth | Local JWT login with seeded users | See [Authentication & Authorization](#authentication--authorization). |
118	| Orchestration | docker-compose | Runs the services and seeds the data locally. |
119	
120	**Shared types.** A shared Pydantic package in the same repository holds the request and response types. The API and the CLI import the same types. The package depends only on Pydantic, not on FastAPI or SQLAlchemy. There is no generated OpenAPI client, so there is no regeneration step.
121	
122	## Data model
123	
124	![Entity diagram](entities.png)
125	
126	Each entity has an `org_id`. See [Tenant isolation](#tenant-isolation).
127	
128	### Conventions
129	- `id` is a UUID primary key. The API paths and the CLI use it. Users and slots also have [short references](#short-references).
130	- Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. Parent tables have `UNIQUE(org_id, id)` for composite foreign keys.
131	- Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. The tables below do not show them.
132	- Fields marked *(derived)* are not stored. The API computes them at query time.
133	
134	### Organization
135	The tenant root.
136	
137	| Field | Type | Notes |
138	|-------|------|-------|
139	| id | uuid | PK |
140	| name | text | |
141	
142	### User
143	
144	| Field | Type | Notes |
145	|-------|------|-------|
146	| id | uuid | PK |
147	| org_id | uuid | FK to organization |
148	| username | text | Globally unique. `mc login --user` uses it. |
149	| display_name | text | |
150	| role | enum | `DIRECTOR`, `LEAD`, `CREW`. One role per user. |
151	
152	### Skill
153	The skill catalogue of the org.
154	
155	| Field | Type | Notes |
156	|-------|------|-------|
157	| id | uuid | PK |
158	| org_id | uuid | FK to organization |
159	| name | text | `UNIQUE(org_id, name)` |
160	| description | text | Optional |
161	
162	### CrewSkill
163	The skill profile of a crew member. It links a user to a skill.
164	
165	| Field | Type | Notes |
166	|-------|------|-------|
167	| org_id | uuid | |
168	| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user |
169	| skill_id | uuid | `(org_id, skill_id)` to skill |
170	| level | smallint | `CHECK` 1 to 5 |
171	
172	- The PK is `(user_id, skill_id)`.
173	- The service layer checks that the user has the role `CREW`.
174	
175	### Unavailability
176	
177	| Field | Type | Notes |
178	|-------|------|-------|
179	| id | uuid | PK. `mc profile availability remove id` uses it. |
180	| org_id | uuid | |
181	| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user |
182	| start_date | date | |
183	| end_date | date | `CHECK end_date >= start_date`. The range includes both dates. |
184	| reason | enum | Examples: `HOLIDAY`, `SICK`, `MEETING`. The API does not show the reason to leads. |
185	
186	### Mission
187	
188	| Field | Type | Notes |
189	|-------|------|-------|
190	| id | uuid | PK |
191	| org_id | uuid | |
192	| title | text | |
193	| description | text | Optional |
194	| lead_id | uuid | `(org_id, lead_id)` to user. The service layer checks the role `LEAD` or `DIRECTOR`. |
195	| status | enum | `DRAFT`, `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `APPROVED`, `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED` |
196	| start_date | date | |
197	| end_date | date | `CHECK end_date >= start_date` |
198	| approved_by | uuid | Optional. `(org_id, approved_by)` to user. A minimal audit trail until the P1 audit log. |
199	| approved_at | timestamptz | Optional. The API clears `approved_by` and `approved_at` when the lead withdraws the mission from APPROVED to DRAFT. |
200	| requires_additional_director | bool *(derived)* | True if the current role of the lead is `DIRECTOR`. Never stored. |
201	
202	### MissionRequirement
203	A slot of a mission: one skill with a minimum level.
204	
205	| Field | Type | Notes |
206	|-------|------|-------|
207	| id | uuid | PK |
208	| org_id | uuid | |
209	| mission_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id)` to mission |
210	| position | smallint | Partial unique index on `(mission_id, position) WHERE archived_at IS NULL`. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. |
211	| skill_id | uuid | `(org_id, skill_id)` to skill |
212	| min_level | smallint | `CHECK` 1 to 5 |
213	| archived_at | timestamptz | Optional. Set when the lead deletes the slot. |
214	
215	- The lead deletes a slot only in DRAFT. The API archives the slot and does not delete the row. Assignment history keeps its reference to the slot.
216	- Archived slots are not part of the mission. The matcher, the invite and the start guard ignore them.
217	- The table also has `UNIQUE(org_id, mission_id, id)`. The assignment references this key.
218	
219	### Assignment
220	
221	| Field | Type | Notes |
222	|-------|------|-------|
223	| id | uuid | PK |
224	| org_id | uuid | |
225	| mission_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id)` to mission |
226	| requirement_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id, requirement_id)` to mission_requirement. The slot belongs to the same mission. |
227	| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user. The service layer checks the role `CREW`. |
228	| status | enum | `INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `DECLINED`, `CANCELLED` |
229	| responded_at | timestamptz | Optional |
230	
231	- Partial unique index on `(mission_id, user_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per crew member and mission.
232	- Partial unique index on `(requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per slot.
233	- The service layer prevents double booking with a row lock. See [Assignment states](#assignment-states).
234	
235	### Derived values
236	The DB does not store these values. The API computes them at query time.
237	
238	| Value | Source |
239	|-------|--------|
240	| Workload | Booked mission days of INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments in a time window before and after the mission. The window (example: 90 days) is a code constant. |
241	| Decliner exclusion | DECLINED assignments of the mission. The API never deletes them, because the matcher reads them. |
242	| Additional director flag | The current role of the mission lead |
243	
244	## Mission lifecycle workflow
245	### Mission states
246	
247	```mermaid
248	stateDiagram-v2
249	    [*] --> DRAFT: create (lead)
250	    DRAFT --> APPROVAL_REQUIRED: submit (lead)
251	    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> APPROVED: approve (director)
252	    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> DRAFT: reject (director) / withdraw (lead)
253	    APPROVED --> DRAFT: withdraw (lead)
254	    APPROVED --> ACTIVE: start (lead)
255	    ACTIVE --> COMPLETED: complete (lead)
256	    DRAFT --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
257	    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
258	    APPROVED --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
259	    ACTIVE --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
260	    COMPLETED --> [*]
261	    CANCELLED --> [*]
262	```
263	
264	| State | Description |
265	|-------|-------------|
266	| DRAFT | The lead creates and edits the mission and its slots, and runs the matcher preview. If the lead is a director, the mission shows that it needs an additional director for approval. |
267	| APPROVAL_REQUIRED | The mission details are final. A director sees the matcher preview and approves or rejects. A rejection returns the mission to DRAFT without a comment. The lead can withdraw the mission to DRAFT. |
268	| APPROVED | The lead staffs the mission and invites crew members. To change details, the lead withdraws the mission to DRAFT. All INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments then become CANCELLED. The API clears `approved_by` and `approved_at`. |
269	| ACTIVE | The lead started the mission. Guard: each slot has an ACCEPTED assignment. |
270	| COMPLETED | The lead completed the mission. |
271	| CANCELLED | The lead cancelled the mission, without a reason. All states except COMPLETED can go to CANCELLED. All INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED. |
272	
273	**Rules**
274	- The lead can edit a mission only in DRAFT.
275	- Staffing changes need no new approval. Example: the lead replaces a crew member who declined.
276	- The code holds the allowed transitions as `action -> (from, to)`. The route of each action checks the actor. This is the extension point for approval workflow customization (P2).
277	- P0 uses one director approval. A later version can store approval configurations in the DB.
278	- Invites happen only after approval. This way, unfunded missions do not reserve scarce skills.
279	- There is no separate staffing state. The assignment states show the staffing progress of an APPROVED mission.
280	
281	### Mission requirements
282	A mission has slots. A slot is one skill with a minimum proficiency level. A crew member fills a maximum of one slot per mission.
283	
284	The lead deletes a slot only in DRAFT. The API archives the slot (soft delete), so the assignment history keeps its reference. The matcher, the invite and the start guard ignore archived slots. See [MissionRequirement](#missionrequirement).
285	
286	### Assignment states
287	
288	```mermaid
289	stateDiagram-v2
290	    [*] --> INVITED: invite (lead, mission APPROVED)
291	    INVITED --> ACCEPTED: accept (crew member)
292	    INVITED --> DECLINED: decline (crew member)
293	    INVITED --> CANCELLED: mission back to DRAFT or cancelled
294	    ACCEPTED --> CANCELLED: mission back to DRAFT or cancelled
295	```
296	
297	| State | Description |
298	|-------|-------------|
299	| INVITED | The lead invited the crew member. This is possible only when the mission is APPROVED. |
300	| ACCEPTED | The crew member accepted. |
301	| DECLINED | The crew member declined. The slot is open again and the lead runs the matcher again. The matcher never suggests this crew member for this mission again. The rematch in APPROVED is deferred (see [Deferred](#deferred)). Until then, the lead invites another crew member by name. |
302	| CANCELLED | The mission went back to DRAFT or the lead cancelled it. The crew member is available again. |
303	
304	The API checks the invite in this order. The first failed check gives the error.
305	
306	1. The mission exists in the org of the lead (404).
307	2. The lead owns the mission (403).
308	3. The mission is APPROVED (409).
309	4. The slot exists (422).
310	5. The crew member exists (422).
311	6. The user has the CREW role (422).
312	7. The slot has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (409).
313	8. The crew member has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on this mission (409).
314	9. The crew member did not decline this mission (409).
315	10. The crew member has the skill at the minimum level (409).
316	11. The crew member has no leave that overlaps the mission (409).
317	12. The crew member has no double booking (409).
318	
319	When more than one leave entry or mission overlaps, the error names the one with the earliest start date.
320	
321	The API checks for double booking at invite and at accept. The service locks the user row of the crew member (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`). In the same transaction, it checks for date overlap with INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments. A DB constraint is not possible, because the assignment does not hold the mission dates.
322	
323	Accept and decline check in this order: the mission exists in the org (404), the crew member has an assignment on the mission (404), the assignment is INVITED (409). Accept then checks double booking with the other missions (409). Accept does not check the skill or the leave again.
324	
325	### Profile conflicts
326	The API rejects a crew profile change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment. The error response names the conflict.
327	
328	| Change | Conflict |
329	|--------|----------|
330	| Add unavailability | The unavailability overlaps the dates of the mission. |
331	| Lower a skill level | The new level is below the minimum level of the slot. |
332	| Remove a skill | The slot requires the skill. |
333	
334	## Authentication & Authorization
335	### Authentication
336	- A user logs in with a seeded user: `mc login --user username`. The API issues a local JWT.
337	- The JWT carries only the `user_id`. The API loads the org and the role from the DB on each request.
338	- Role changes and revocation apply immediately. The cost is one primary key lookup per request.
339	
340	### Roles
341	Each user has one role. The hierarchy is Director > Lead: a director can do all that a lead can do. Crew members are not part of this hierarchy.
342	
343	A director acts only on their own missions. A director cannot act on the mission of another lead. The only exception is approve or reject.
344	
345	| Action | Director | Lead | Crew member |
346	|--------|----------|------|-------------|
347	| Create and edit own missions (DRAFT only) | Yes | Yes | No |
348	| Run the matcher on own missions (preview in DRAFT) | Yes | Yes | No |
349	| Invite crew to own missions (APPROVED only) | Yes | Yes | No |
350	| Approve or reject missions | Yes, not own missions | No | No |
351	| View all missions and crew of the org | Yes | Yes, leave shows as "unavailable" without reason | No |
352	| Edit org settings (skills) | Yes | No | No |
353	| View own assignments, history and mission details | No | No | Yes |
354	| Accept or decline own assignments | No | No | Yes |
355	| View and edit own profile: skills and unavailability | No | No | Yes |
356	
357	### Approval rules
358	- A mission lead never approves their own mission.
359	- A director who leads a mission needs a second director for approval.
360	- The API and the CLI flag this at mission creation: the mission needs an additional director.
361	- The API derives the flag from the current role of the lead. The DB never stores the flag.
362	
363	### Assignment rules
364	- Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead or a director is never a crew member.
365	- The service layer checks this rule. The composite foreign keys do not cover it.
366	
367	### Error format
368	The API enforces permissions. For a forbidden action in the own org, the API returns 403 with the role and the rule. The CLI shows both. See [Tenant isolation](#tenant-isolation) for 404 rules.
369	
370	## Tenant isolation
371	Each org is a tenant. Data must never leak across tenants.
372	
373	- Each user belongs to one org.
374	- Each query goes through an org-scoped data-access layer. The layer compares the org of the user with the org of the data.
375	- The layer looks up each referenced ID (for example `skill_id`, `crew_id`) with an org filter. A cross-org ID returns no data.
376	
377	### Composite foreign keys
378	Composite foreign keys are a second layer for writes. The DB rejects cross-org links even if the data-access layer has a bug.
379	
380	- Each tenant table has `org_id`. Parent tables have `UNIQUE(org_id, id)`.
381	- Child tables reference `(org_id, x_id) -> parent(org_id, id)`:
382	
383	| Child | Parent |
384	|-------|--------|
385	| assignment | mission, user |
386	| assignment `(org_id, mission_id, requirement_id)` | mission_requirement `(org_id, mission_id, id)`, so the slot belongs to the same mission |
387	| mission_requirement | mission, skill |
388	| crew_skill | user, skill |
389	| unavailability | user |
390	| mission.lead_id | user |
391	| mission.approved_by | user |
392	
393	Composite foreign keys do not protect reads. Reads rely only on the data-access layer. Postgres RLS as a second layer for reads is P2.
394	
395	### Error rules
396	
397	| Case | Response |
398	|------|----------|
399	| The resource does not exist | 404 |
400	| The resource exists in another org | 404. The response never shows that the resource exists. |
401	| The resource exists in the own org, but the role has no access | 403 with role and rule |
402	
403	### Verification
404	The happy path tests include cross-org access checks for each build step.
405	
406	## Matching engine
407	The matcher fills each slot with one crew member. A slot is one skill with a minimum level.
408	
409	### Filters
410	The matcher includes a crew member in the selection set only if all conditions are true:
411	- The crew member is in the same org.
412	- The crew member has the skill at the minimum level or higher.
413	- The crew member has no unavailability, INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment in the mission timeframe.
414	- The crew member has not declined this mission.
415	
416	### Ranking
417	The matcher ranks the candidates of a slot in this strict order. A later rule applies only at a full tie of the earlier rules.
418	1. **Proficiency is closest to the minimum (gap).** The gap is `level - min_level`. Experts stay free for missions with higher proficiency requirements.
419	2. **Scarcity is lower.** Scarcity is the max of `1 / holders` over the other skills of the crew member, without the slot skill. `holders` counts the CREW members of the org with the skill at any level. A crew member with no other skill has scarcity 0. The matcher keeps the holders of a rare skill free.
420	3. **Workload is lower.** Workload is the number of booked mission days (INVITED and ACCEPTED) in a window of 90 days before and after the mission. Workload is only a tie breaker. A workload cap is P2.
421	4. **The username is first in alphabetical order.** This rule makes each result deterministic.
422	
423	### Slot assignment
424	- The matcher assigns all slots together, not one by one.
425	- scipy `linear_sum_assignment` solves a slots x candidates cost matrix. A big cost marks the ineligible pairs, so the solver fills the maximum number of slots first.
426	- Rematching fills only open slots. An open slot has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment.
427	
428	### Availability
429	Crew members manage unavailable time slots, not available periods. Examples are holiday leave, sick leave and internal meetings. The time slots use dates only.
430	
431	### Deferred
432	- P1: rank breakdown per suggestion, and reasons for excluded crew members.
433	- P1: rematch of open slots (requirement 19, build step 7). The design keeps this rule. The build deferred it: slice 5 of the staffing plan is not built. The matcher preview runs on an APPROVED mission and lists only open slots. Today the preview runs only in DRAFT, and the permission row "Run the matcher on own missions" reads "preview in DRAFT". The lead invites by name in APPROVED. The decliner filter of the matcher already works, so the rematch needs no schema or API change.
434	- P2: gap report when no match exists, resource constraints, rest buffer, mission priority.
435	
436	## CLI
437	The CLI command is `mc`. It calls the API and stores the token locally after login.
438	
439	### Commands v0
440	
441	| Workflow | Command |
442	|----------|---------|
443	| Login | `mc login --user username`, `mc logout` |
444	| Missions list | `mc missions list` |
445	| Mission detail | `mc missions show <mission-id>` |
446	| Mission lifecycle | `mc missions create\|edit\|submit\|withdraw\|approve\|reject\|cancel\|start\|complete` |
447	| Matcher | `mc missions match <mission-id>` |
448	| Invite (APPROVED only) | `mc missions invite <mission-id> --slot 1 --crew username` |
449	| My assignments (crew), current and history | `mc assignments list` |
450	| Respond to assignment | `mc assignments accept\|decline <mission-id>` |
451	| My profile (crew) | `mc profile show` |
452	| Skills | `mc profile skills set <skill-id> --level n`, `mc profile skills remove <skill-id>` |
453	| Availability | `mc profile availability list`, `add --from date --to date`, `remove id` |
454	
455	The CLI shows table views.
456	
457	### Short references
458	The API paths use UUIDs. The CLI uses UUIDs for missions and skills. Each entity in an API response contains the `id` and, if it has one, the short reference. A DB unique constraint enforces each short reference.
459	
460	| Resource | Key | Constraint |
461	|----------|-----|------------|
462	| User | `username` | Globally unique, because `mc login --user` has no org context. The CLI references crew members by username. |
463	| Slot | Position in the mission (1, 2, 3) | Partial unique index on `(mission_id, position) WHERE archived_at IS NULL`. Partial unique index on assignment `(requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per slot. |
464	| Assignment | Mission UUID | Partial unique index: one INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment per `(mission_id, user_id)` |
465	
466	#### P1: Mission and skill short references
467	P1 adds short references for missions and skills in the CLI.
468	
469	| Resource | Key | Constraint |
470	|----------|-----|------------|
471	| Mission | `MSN-<n>` per org | `UNIQUE(org_id, number)`. See below. |
472	| Skill | `slug` | `UNIQUE(org_id, slug)`. The API rejects a duplicate slug with a clear error. There is no automatic suffix. |
473	
474	The API gets the next mission number with `UPDATE org SET mission_seq = mission_seq + 1 ... RETURNING` in the same transaction. The row lock serializes concurrent creates, so numbers do not collide.
475	
476	## Changes
477	
478	| Date | Change | Reason |
479	|------|--------|--------|
480	| 2026-10-11 | Add build step 10, org crew view. The demo becomes step 11. | Requirement 11 had no build step. Step 9 covers only the own profile of a crew member. |
481	| 2026-10-11 | Decide the matcher cost order, the scarcity rule and the solver. | Build step 5 had to evaluate the scarcity term and scipy. |
482	| 2026-10-11 | Key the transition table by action. | Withdraw and reject both go from APPROVAL_REQUIRED to DRAFT, with different actors. |
483	| 2026-10-11 | Defer the matcher preview on APPROVED missions (rematch of open slots). Build step 7 ships invite, accept, decline and the double booking check without it. | The lead can invite by name. The rematch needs no schema or API change and follows later. |
484

file.content:
# Mission Control MVP v0

## Background
The customer is the operations team of an organization (org). An org can be a space agency or a private company.

Mission leads spend hours to cross-reference skill profiles, availability calendars and existing commitments. Mission staffing is the bottleneck. Mission Control finds qualified and available crew members for a mission and makes sure that they are not overloaded.

| User | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Mission lead (power user) | Manages missions. Staffs them with qualified and available crew members. |
| Director | Approves or rejects missions. Oversees the org. Manages org settings (skills). |
| Crew member | Manages their profile (skills and availability). Accepts or declines assignments. |

## Requirements
### P0
P0 is the first version that is ready to pitch to a customer.

**Delivery**
1. A reviewer clones the GitHub repository and runs it locally in minutes. The repository contains setup instructions, demo seed data, this design document, the API and the CLI.
2. The repository contains evidence of verification: test output and a scripted CLI demo.
3. The seed data has 2 orgs and 2 directors in one org. It has enough crew members to show the matcher trade-offs: experts against closest fit, leave and workload.

**Auth and tenant**

4. Each org is a separate tenant with exclusive data access. The data-access layer and composite foreign keys enforce this.
5. Each user has one role: director, lead or crew member. The API enforces the role permissions.
6. A user logs in to the CLI as a seeded user (`mc login --user username`).
7. For a forbidden action, the CLI shows a clear error with the role and the rule.

**Mission lifecycle**

8. Each mission needs approval. The lead submits the mission to a director.
9. The director approves or rejects the mission. The approval view shows the matcher preview.
10. Crew members accept or decline assignments.
11. Directors see the whole org: all missions and all crew members (API and CLI).

**Crew and skills**

12. Crew members manage their skill profile via the CLI. They list, add, update and remove their own skills from the org catalogue, with a proficiency level.
13. Crew members manage their availability via the CLI. They list, add and remove their own unavailability.
14. Crew members see their own assignments with history (past, declined), their profile and the mission details. They accept or decline assignments.
15. Each org has its own set of skills. P0 seeds the skills. P1 adds skill editing.

**Matching**

16. The matcher suggests crew members for a mission. The inputs are skills, availability and workload.
17. The lead runs a read-only matcher preview in DRAFT to check that the mission can be staffed.
18. The lead invites crew members only when the mission is APPROVED.
19. Rematching fills only open slots. It never suggests a crew member who declined this mission.

**CLI**

20. The primary workflows run through the CLI. See [CLI](#cli).

**Quality**

21. Tests cover the happy path per workflow: lifecycle, matcher, invites and responses, crew profile.
22. Cross-org access checks make sure that resources of another org return 404.
23. A scripted end-to-end CLI demo runs the full mission lifecycle over the seed data.

#### Build order
Each step ends with its happy path test and its cross-org check. Each step is one or more commits.

1. Skeleton: docker-compose Postgres, FastAPI app, Alembic, Typer entry point, README run steps.
2. Data model, first migration and seed data: 2 orgs, 2 directors in one org, leads, crew, skills, leave, existing assignments for workload.
3. Auth and tenant: `mc login`, JWT with `user_id`, per-request load of user, org and role, org-scoped data-access layer, RBAC error format.
4. Missions in DRAFT: create, edit, slots, list, show.
5. Matcher preview: filters, ranking, slot assignment. `mc missions match`.
6. Approval: submit, withdraw, approve, reject. No self approval, additional director flag, matcher preview in the approval view.
7. Staffing: invite, `mc assignments list / accept / decline`, double booking check, decliner exclusion on rematch.
8. Remaining transitions: withdraw from APPROVED to DRAFT, start (with guard), complete, cancel. Assignment cancellation.
9. Crew profile: `mc profile show`, skills, availability.
10. Org crew view: directors and leads list and show the crew members of the org (requirement 11). Leads see leave as "unavailable" without the reason.
11. Scripted end-to-end CLI demo and test results in the README.

### P1
P1 extends the MVP if time permits in this session.

1. Directors manage the org skill catalogue.
2. Mission audit logs.
3. Decision insights for the lead: why the matcher excluded a crew member.
4. Rank breakdown per suggestion: why a crew member is the best fit for the slot.
5. Short references for missions (`MSN-<n>`) and skills (`slug`) in the CLI. See [Short references](#short-references).

### P2
P2 is out of scope for this session.

| Area | Item |
|------|------|
| Auth and tenant | Noisy-neighbour protection and uneven org sizes |
| | Real IdP (OIDC), login and signup |
| | Postgres RLS as a second layer for reads |
| | User and role management |
| Mission lifecycle | Approval workflow customization |
| | Crew members withdraw after they accept |
| | Reject with comment, cancel with reason |
| | Reassign the lead of a mission |
| Crew and skills | Edit and archive skills |
| | Verification of self-assessed proficiency |
| Matching | Additional resource constraints |
| | Report of skill gaps and possible resolutions when no match exists |
| | Rest buffer between missions |
| | Mission priority |
| | Optimization for large orgs |
| Operations | CI/CD |
| | Scalability, observability, IaC, offline jobs |

## Tech stack
The API and the CLI use one language (Python). This keeps the stack small.

| Component | Choice | Reason |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| CLI | Typer, httpx, Rich | Typed commands, generated help, readable tables. The CLI calls the API and stores the token locally after login. |
| API | FastAPI, Pydantic | Typed API with generated OpenAPI docs. |
| Data access | SQLAlchemy, Alembic | Safe DB access with migrations. |
| Database | Postgres | |
| Auth | Local JWT login with seeded users | See [Authentication & Authorization](#authentication--authorization). |
| Orchestration | docker-compose | Runs the services and seeds the data locally. |

**Shared types.** A shared Pydantic package in the same repository holds the request and response types. The API and the CLI import the same types. The package depends only on Pydantic, not on FastAPI or SQLAlchemy. There is no generated OpenAPI client, so there is no regeneration step.

## Data model

![Entity diagram](entities.png)

Each entity has an `org_id`. See [Tenant isolation](#tenant-isolation).

### Conventions
- `id` is a UUID primary key. The API paths and the CLI use it. Users and slots also have [short references](#short-references).
- Each tenant table has `org_id NOT NULL`. Parent tables have `UNIQUE(org_id, id)` for composite foreign keys.
- Each table has `created_at` and `updated_at`. The tables below do not show them.
- Fields marked *(derived)* are not stored. The API computes them at query time.

### Organization
The tenant root.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| name | text | |

### User

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| org_id | uuid | FK to organization |
| username | text | Globally unique. `mc login --user` uses it. |
| display_name | text | |
| role | enum | `DIRECTOR`, `LEAD`, `CREW`. One role per user. |

### Skill
The skill catalogue of the org.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| org_id | uuid | FK to organization |
| name | text | `UNIQUE(org_id, name)` |
| description | text | Optional |

### CrewSkill
The skill profile of a crew member. It links a user to a skill.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| org_id | uuid | |
| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user |
| skill_id | uuid | `(org_id, skill_id)` to skill |
| level | smallint | `CHECK` 1 to 5 |

- The PK is `(user_id, skill_id)`.
- The service layer checks that the user has the role `CREW`.

### Unavailability

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK. `mc profile availability remove id` uses it. |
| org_id | uuid | |
| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user |
| start_date | date | |
| end_date | date | `CHECK end_date >= start_date`. The range includes both dates. |
| reason | enum | Examples: `HOLIDAY`, `SICK`, `MEETING`. The API does not show the reason to leads. |

### Mission

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| org_id | uuid | |
| title | text | |
| description | text | Optional |
| lead_id | uuid | `(org_id, lead_id)` to user. The service layer checks the role `LEAD` or `DIRECTOR`. |
| status | enum | `DRAFT`, `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `APPROVED`, `ACTIVE`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED` |
| start_date | date | |
| end_date | date | `CHECK end_date >= start_date` |
| approved_by | uuid | Optional. `(org_id, approved_by)` to user. A minimal audit trail until the P1 audit log. |
| approved_at | timestamptz | Optional. The API clears `approved_by` and `approved_at` when the lead withdraws the mission from APPROVED to DRAFT. |
| requires_additional_director | bool *(derived)* | True if the current role of the lead is `DIRECTOR`. Never stored. |

### MissionRequirement
A slot of a mission: one skill with a minimum level.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| org_id | uuid | |
| mission_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id)` to mission |
| position | smallint | Partial unique index on `(mission_id, position) WHERE archived_at IS NULL`. A new slot can use the position of an archived slot. |
| skill_id | uuid | `(org_id, skill_id)` to skill |
| min_level | smallint | `CHECK` 1 to 5 |
| archived_at | timestamptz | Optional. Set when the lead deletes the slot. |

- The lead deletes a slot only in DRAFT. The API archives the slot and does not delete the row. Assignment history keeps its reference to the slot.
- Archived slots are not part of the mission. The matcher, the invite and the start guard ignore them.
- The table also has `UNIQUE(org_id, mission_id, id)`. The assignment references this key.

### Assignment

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| id | uuid | PK |
| org_id | uuid | |
| mission_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id)` to mission |
| requirement_id | uuid | `(org_id, mission_id, requirement_id)` to mission_requirement. The slot belongs to the same mission. |
| user_id | uuid | `(org_id, user_id)` to user. The service layer checks the role `CREW`. |
| status | enum | `INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `DECLINED`, `CANCELLED` |
| responded_at | timestamptz | Optional |

- Partial unique index on `(mission_id, user_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per crew member and mission.
- Partial unique index on `(requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per slot.
- The service layer prevents double booking with a row lock. See [Assignment states](#assignment-states).

### Derived values
The DB does not store these values. The API computes them at query time.

| Value | Source |
|-------|--------|
| Workload | Booked mission days of INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments in a time window before and after the mission. The window (example: 90 days) is a code constant. |
| Decliner exclusion | DECLINED assignments of the mission. The API never deletes them, because the matcher reads them. |
| Additional director flag | The current role of the mission lead |

## Mission lifecycle workflow
### Mission states

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> DRAFT: create (lead)
    DRAFT --> APPROVAL_REQUIRED: submit (lead)
    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> APPROVED: approve (director)
    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> DRAFT: reject (director) / withdraw (lead)
    APPROVED --> DRAFT: withdraw (lead)
    APPROVED --> ACTIVE: start (lead)
    ACTIVE --> COMPLETED: complete (lead)
    DRAFT --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
    APPROVAL_REQUIRED --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
    APPROVED --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
    ACTIVE --> CANCELLED: cancel (lead)
    COMPLETED --> [*]
    CANCELLED --> [*]
```

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| DRAFT | The lead creates and edits the mission and its slots, and runs the matcher preview. If the lead is a director, the mission shows that it needs an additional director for approval. |
| APPROVAL_REQUIRED | The mission details are final. A director sees the matcher preview and approves or rejects. A rejection returns the mission to DRAFT without a comment. The lead can withdraw the mission to DRAFT. |
| APPROVED | The lead staffs the mission and invites crew members. To change details, the lead withdraws the mission to DRAFT. All INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments then become CANCELLED. The API clears `approved_by` and `approved_at`. |
| ACTIVE | The lead started the mission. Guard: each slot has an ACCEPTED assignment. |
| COMPLETED | The lead completed the mission. |
| CANCELLED | The lead cancelled the mission, without a reason. All states except COMPLETED can go to CANCELLED. All INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED. |

**Rules**
- The lead can edit a mission only in DRAFT.
- Staffing changes need no new approval. Example: the lead replaces a crew member who declined.
- The code holds the allowed transitions as `action -> (from, to)`. The route of each action checks the actor. This is the extension point for approval workflow customization (P2).
- P0 uses one director approval. A later version can store approval configurations in the DB.
- Invites happen only after approval. This way, unfunded missions do not reserve scarce skills.
- There is no separate staffing state. The assignment states show the staffing progress of an APPROVED mission.

### Mission requirements
A mission has slots. A slot is one skill with a minimum proficiency level. A crew member fills a maximum of one slot per mission.

The lead deletes a slot only in DRAFT. The API archives the slot (soft delete), so the assignment history keeps its reference. The matcher, the invite and the start guard ignore archived slots. See [MissionRequirement](#missionrequirement).

### Assignment states

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> INVITED: invite (lead, mission APPROVED)
    INVITED --> ACCEPTED: accept (crew member)
    INVITED --> DECLINED: decline (crew member)
    INVITED --> CANCELLED: mission back to DRAFT or cancelled
    ACCEPTED --> CANCELLED: mission back to DRAFT or cancelled
```

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| INVITED | The lead invited the crew member. This is possible only when the mission is APPROVED. |
| ACCEPTED | The crew member accepted. |
| DECLINED | The crew member declined. The slot is open again and the lead runs the matcher again. The matcher never suggests this crew member for this mission again. The rematch in APPROVED is deferred (see [Deferred](#deferred)). Until then, the lead invites another crew member by name. |
| CANCELLED | The mission went back to DRAFT or the lead cancelled it. The crew member is available again. |

The API checks the invite in this order. The first failed check gives the error.

1. The mission exists in the org of the lead (404).
2. The lead owns the mission (403).
3. The mission is APPROVED (409).
4. The slot exists (422).
5. The crew member exists (422).
6. The user has the CREW role (422).
7. The slot has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (409).
8. The crew member has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on this mission (409).
9. The crew member did not decline this mission (409).
10. The crew member has the skill at the minimum level (409).
11. The crew member has no leave that overlaps the mission (409).
12. The crew member has no double booking (409).

When more than one leave entry or mission overlaps, the error names the one with the earliest start date.

The API checks for double booking at invite and at accept. The service locks the user row of the crew member (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`). In the same transaction, it checks for date overlap with INVITED and ACCEPTED assignments. A DB constraint is not possible, because the assignment does not hold the mission dates.

Accept and decline check in this order: the mission exists in the org (404), the crew member has an assignment on the mission (404), the assignment is INVITED (409). Accept then checks double booking with the other missions (409). Accept does not check the skill or the leave again.

### Profile conflicts
The API rejects a crew profile change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment. The error response names the conflict.

| Change | Conflict |
|--------|----------|
| Add unavailability | The unavailability overlaps the dates of the mission. |
| Lower a skill level | The new level is below the minimum level of the slot. |
| Remove a skill | The slot requires the skill. |

## Authentication & Authorization
### Authentication
- A user logs in with a seeded user: `mc login --user username`. The API issues a local JWT.
- The JWT carries only the `user_id`. The API loads the org and the role from the DB on each request.
- Role changes and revocation apply immediately. The cost is one primary key lookup per request.

### Roles
Each user has one role. The hierarchy is Director > Lead: a director can do all that a lead can do. Crew members are not part of this hierarchy.

A director acts only on their own missions. A director cannot act on the mission of another lead. The only exception is approve or reject.

| Action | Director | Lead | Crew member |
|--------|----------|------|-------------|
| Create and edit own missions (DRAFT only) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Run the matcher on own missions (preview in DRAFT) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Invite crew to own missions (APPROVED only) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Approve or reject missions | Yes, not own missions | No | No |
| View all missions and crew of the org | Yes | Yes, leave shows as "unavailable" without reason | No |
| Edit org settings (skills) | Yes | No | No |
| View own assignments, history and mission details | No | No | Yes |
| Accept or decline own assignments | No | No | Yes |
| View and edit own profile: skills and unavailability | No | No | Yes |

### Approval rules
- A mission lead never approves their own mission.
- A director who leads a mission needs a second director for approval.
- The API and the CLI flag this at mission creation: the mission needs an additional director.
- The API derives the flag from the current role of the lead. The DB never stores the flag.

### Assignment rules
- Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead or a director is never a crew member.
- The service layer checks this rule. The composite foreign keys do not cover it.

### Error format
The API enforces permissions. For a forbidden action in the own org, the API returns 403 with the role and the rule. The CLI shows both. See [Tenant isolation](#tenant-isolation) for 404 rules.

## Tenant isolation
Each org is a tenant. Data must never leak across tenants.

- Each user belongs to one org.
- Each query goes through an org-scoped data-access layer. The layer compares the org of the user with the org of the data.
- The layer looks up each referenced ID (for example `skill_id`, `crew_id`) with an org filter. A cross-org ID returns no data.

### Composite foreign keys
Composite foreign keys are a second layer for writes. The DB rejects cross-org links even if the data-access layer has a bug.

- Each tenant table has `org_id`. Parent tables have `UNIQUE(org_id, id)`.
- Child tables reference `(org_id, x_id) -> parent(org_id, id)`:

| Child | Parent |
|-------|--------|
| assignment | mission, user |
| assignment `(org_id, mission_id, requirement_id)` | mission_requirement `(org_id, mission_id, id)`, so the slot belongs to the same mission |
| mission_requirement | mission, skill |
| crew_skill | user, skill |
| unavailability | user |
| mission.lead_id | user |
| mission.approved_by | user |

Composite foreign keys do not protect reads. Reads rely only on the data-access layer. Postgres RLS as a second layer for reads is P2.

### Error rules

| Case | Response |
|------|----------|
| The resource does not exist | 404 |
| The resource exists in another org | 404. The response never shows that the resource exists. |
| The resource exists in the own org, but the role has no access | 403 with role and rule |

### Verification
The happy path tests include cross-org access checks for each build step.

## Matching engine
The matcher fills each slot with one crew member. A slot is one skill with a minimum level.

### Filters
The matcher includes a crew member in the selection set only if all conditions are true:
- The crew member is in the same org.
- The crew member has the skill at the minimum level or higher.
- The crew member has no unavailability, INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment in the mission timeframe.
- The crew member has not declined this mission.

### Ranking
The matcher ranks the candidates of a slot in this strict order. A later rule applies only at a full tie of the earlier rules.
1. **Proficiency is closest to the minimum (gap).** The gap is `level - min_level`. Experts stay free for missions with higher proficiency requirements.
2. **Scarcity is lower.** Scarcity is the max of `1 / holders` over the other skills of the crew member, without the slot skill. `holders` counts the CREW members of the org with the skill at any level. A crew member with no other skill has scarcity 0. The matcher keeps the holders of a rare skill free.
3. **Workload is lower.** Workload is the number of booked mission days (INVITED and ACCEPTED) in a window of 90 days before and after the mission. Workload is only a tie breaker. A workload cap is P2.
4. **The username is first in alphabetical order.** This rule makes each result deterministic.

### Slot assignment
- The matcher assigns all slots together, not one by one.
- scipy `linear_sum_assignment` solves a slots x candidates cost matrix. A big cost marks the ineligible pairs, so the solver fills the maximum number of slots first.
- Rematching fills only open slots. An open slot has no INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment.

### Availability
Crew members manage unavailable time slots, not available periods. Examples are holiday leave, sick leave and internal meetings. The time slots use dates only.

### Deferred
- P1: rank breakdown per suggestion, and reasons for excluded crew members.
- P1: rematch of open slots (requirement 19, build step 7). The design keeps this rule. The build deferred it: slice 5 of the staffing plan is not built. The matcher preview runs on an APPROVED mission and lists only open slots. Today the preview runs only in DRAFT, and the permission row "Run the matcher on own missions" reads "preview in DRAFT". The lead invites by name in APPROVED. The decliner filter of the matcher already works, so the rematch needs no schema or API change.
- P2: gap report when no match exists, resource constraints, rest buffer, mission priority.

## CLI
The CLI command is `mc`. It calls the API and stores the token locally after login.

### Commands v0

| Workflow | Command |
|----------|---------|
| Login | `mc login --user username`, `mc logout` |
| Missions list | `mc missions list` |
| Mission detail | `mc missions show <mission-id>` |
| Mission lifecycle | `mc missions create\|edit\|submit\|withdraw\|approve\|reject\|cancel\|start\|complete` |
| Matcher | `mc missions match <mission-id>` |
| Invite (APPROVED only) | `mc missions invite <mission-id> --slot 1 --crew username` |
| My assignments (crew), current and history | `mc assignments list` |
| Respond to assignment | `mc assignments accept\|decline <mission-id>` |
| My profile (crew) | `mc profile show` |
| Skills | `mc profile skills set <skill-id> --level n`, `mc profile skills remove <skill-id>` |
| Availability | `mc profile availability list`, `add --from date --to date`, `remove id` |

The CLI shows table views.

### Short references
The API paths use UUIDs. The CLI uses UUIDs for missions and skills. Each entity in an API response contains the `id` and, if it has one, the short reference. A DB unique constraint enforces each short reference.

| Resource | Key | Constraint |
|----------|-----|------------|
| User | `username` | Globally unique, because `mc login --user` has no org context. The CLI references crew members by username. |
| Slot | Position in the mission (1, 2, 3) | Partial unique index on `(mission_id, position) WHERE archived_at IS NULL`. Partial unique index on assignment `(requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED)`: one active assignment per slot. |
| Assignment | Mission UUID | Partial unique index: one INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment per `(mission_id, user_id)` |

#### P1: Mission and skill short references
P1 adds short references for missions and skills in the CLI.

| Resource | Key | Constraint |
|----------|-----|------------|
| Mission | `MSN-<n>` per org | `UNIQUE(org_id, number)`. See below. |
| Skill | `slug` | `UNIQUE(org_id, slug)`. The API rejects a duplicate slug with a clear error. There is no automatic suffix. |

The API gets the next mission number with `UPDATE org SET mission_seq = mission_seq + 1 ... RETURNING` in the same transaction. The row lock serializes concurrent creates, so numbers do not collide.

## Changes

| Date | Change | Reason |
|------|--------|--------|
| 2026-10-11 | Add build step 10, org crew view. The demo becomes step 11. | Requirement 11 had no build step. Step 9 covers only the own profile of a crew member. |
| 2026-10-11 | Decide the matcher cost order, the scarcity rule and the solver. | Build step 5 had to evaluate the scarcity term and scipy. |
| 2026-10-11 | Key the transition table by action. | Withdraw and reject both go from APPROVAL_REQUIRED to DRAFT, with different actors. |
| 2026-10-11 | Defer the matcher preview on APPROVED missions (rematch of open slots). Build step 7 ships invite, accept, decline and the double booking check without it. | The lead can invite by name. The rematch needs no schema or API change and follows later. |

# Decisions
This file contains my personal decisions and assumptions made based on the BRIEF.md before starting to build the product.

## Who and what
* Customer: An institutions / organizations operations team. Organizations can be space agencies or other private companies. 
* Main or power user: A mission lead. This person manages missions and staffs them with qualified and available staff while ensuring they are not overloaded. 
* Other users: 
  * A director. This person approves missions sent for a approval by the mission lead and oversees the organization. This includes managing organizational settings (skills)
  * A crew member. This person manages their profile (manage their skills and availability) and responds to assingments (accept / decline)
* Today's pain point: Mission leads spend hours cross-referencing skill profiles, availability calendars and existing commitments. Staffing missions efficiently is the bottleneck

## Requirements
### P0: Core requirements enabling first initial version ready to pitch to a customer
#### Delivery
1. Ready version a reviewer can clone and run locally in minutes
    - GitHub repository
    - Setup instructions
    - Seeding initial data - demo
    - Design document written before implementation and used to guide the agent
    - API + CLI
    - Evidence of verification: test output and scripted CLI demo
2. Seed data with 2 orgs and 2 Directors in one org
    - Representative data enough crew so the matcher shows trade-offs (experts vs closest fit, leave, workload)
#### Auth and tenant
3. Multi-Tenant system: Organizations are separate tenants. Exclusive data access
    - Enforced in data-access layer and with composite foreign keys in DB
4. Users have different roles (Director, Lead, Crew member) and role permissions are enforced
    - Login in the CLI with a seeded user (e.g. mc login --user username)
    - CLI shows a clear error for forbidden actions: which role and which rule
    - Actions / Permissions are protected on the API layer
#### Mission lifecycle
5. Initial version of mission lifecycle management
    - Each missions needs approval
    - Leads send for approval to Director
    - Directors approve / reject. The approval view shows the matcher preview
    - Crew members accept/ decline assignment
6. Directors can view the whole org (broad view)
    - All missions
    - All crew members (API + CLI)
#### Crew and skills
7. Crew members have a skill profile and availability and manage them via CLI
    - Skills: list, add, update, remove own skills from the org catalogue with proficiency
    - Availability: list, add, remove own unavailability
8. Crew members see their own assignments incl. history (past, declined), profile and mission and can respond to assignments (accept / decline)
9. Each org has own set of skills
    - Seed data in this phase, editing in P1
#### Matching
10. Smart suggestions of crew members for a mission
    - Inputs: Skills, availability, workload
    - Lead can run a readonly preview in draft status to check the mission can be staffed before submit
    - Invites only when mission is approved
    - Rematching only fills open slots and never suggests a member who declined this mission
#### CLI
11. Primary workflows run through the CLI: login, missions list /detail, create/ edit, submit, approve / reject, matching preview and invites, my assignments and history (crew), accept / decline, my profile and availability (crew).
#### Quality
12. Tests: minimal happy path only for now
    - Happy path per workflow: lifecycle, matcher, invites and responses, crew profile
    - Cross org access checks: other org's resources return 404
13. Evidence of verification
    - Scripted end-to-end CLI demo over the seed data (full mission lifecycle)
    - Test results documented: Readme?

### P0 build order
Each step ends with its happy path test and cross org check. Each step is one or more commits.
1. Skeleton: docker-compose Postgres, FastAPI app, Alembic, Typer entry point, README run steps
2. Data model + first migration + seed data (2 orgs, 2 directors in one org, leads, crew, skills, leave, existing assignments for workload)
3. Auth and tenant: mc login, JWT with user_id, per request user / org / role load, org scoped data-access layer, RBAC error format
4. Missions in DRAFT: create, edit, slots, list, show
5. Matcher preview: filters, ranking, slot assignment. mc missions match
6. Approval: submit, withdraw, approve, reject. No self approval, additional director flag, preview in approval view
7. Staffing: invite, mc assignments list / accept / decline, double booking check, decliner exclusion on rematch
8. Remaining transitions: withdraw from APPROVED back to draft, start (guard), complete, cancel. Assignment cancellation
9. Crew profile: mc profile show, skills, availability
10. Scripted end-to-end CLI demo + test results in README

### P1: Next extensions: If time permits in this session
#### Crew and skills
1. Directors manage org settings
    - Skill catalogue
#### Mission lifecyle
2. Mission audit logs
#### Matching
3. Decision insights for lead: Excluded members: Why?
4. Rank breakdown per suggestion: Why is this the best person for the slot
#### CLI
5. Short references for missions (`MSN-<n>`) and skills (`slug`), see Short references
...

### P2: Scoped as outside of this session
#### Auth and tenant
1. Noisy-neighbour protection / uneven org sizes in this multi tenant architecture
2. Real idp oidc, login / signup, 
3. Postgres RLS as second layer for reads (composite FKs only protect writes / links)
4. User and role management
#### Mission lifecycle
5. Approval workflow customization
6. Crew members withdraw after accepting
7. Reject with comment, cancel with reason
8. Reassign the lead of a mission
#### Crew and skills
9. Edit / archive skills
10. Verification of self assessed proficiency
#### Matching
11. Additional resource constraints, extending the matching engine
12. No matches and report gap and potential resolutions
13. Rest buffer between missions
14. Mission priority
15. Optimize for larger orgs with lots of staff
#### Operations
16. CI / CD
17. Scalability, Observability, IaC, offline jobs, etc. 

## Ambiguity resolution
1. Different skill taxonomy per org -> Skills owned by each org with fixed proficiency scale (1-5). Skill names are unique per org: UNIQUE(org_id, name)
2. Different approval processes per org -> Initial scope will be one single director approval in code. Later extension to DB stored approval configs
3. Leads cannot approve their own missions -> One role per user with hierarchy Director > Lead, so a director can also lead missions. The mission lead can never approve their own mission. A director who is also leading a mission needs a second director to get approval. On mission creation the API and CLI flag that this mission requires an additional director for approval.
4. Who can be assinged to a mission: Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead is never a crew member and a director is never a crew member. The Director > Lead hierarchy does not include Crew.
5. Directors approve missions -> A mission to approve consists of requirements, timeline and date. Lead can preview the matcher in draft to check the mission can be staffed before submit. The director sees the same matcher preview in the approval view. Invites happen only after approval, so scarce skills are not reserved for unfunded missions. No separate steps for now
6. Changing after approval -> Missions can only be edited in draft. Before changing mission details after a director approved lead needs to withdraw the mission back to draft status. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments are then CANCELLED. Staffing changes (e.g. replacing a declined crew member) are not a change and need no new approval.
7. Availability tracking -> Instead of managing available periods it is more pragmatic to manage unavailable timeslots: holiday leave, sick leave, internal meetings, etc. Dates only. A crew member is blocked by unavailability, invited and accepted assignments.

    - Cross org access checks: other org's resources return 404
13. Evidence of verification
    - Scripted end-to-end CLI demo over the seed data (full mission lifecycle)
    - Test results documented: Readme?

### P0 build order
Each step ends with its happy path test and cross org check. Each step is one or more commits.
1. Skeleton: docker-compose Postgres, FastAPI app, Alembic, Typer entry point, README run steps
2. Data model + first migration + seed data (2 orgs, 2 directors in one org, leads, crew, skills, leave, existing assignments for workload)
3. Auth and tenant: mc login, JWT with user_id, per request user / org / role load, org scoped data-access layer, RBAC error format
4. Missions in DRAFT: create, edit, slots, list, show
5. Matcher preview: filters, ranking, slot assignment. mc missions match
6. Approval: submit, withdraw, approve, reject. No self approval, additional director flag, preview in approval view
7. Staffing: invite, mc assignments list / accept / decline, double booking check, decliner exclusion on rematch
8. Remaining transitions: withdraw from APPROVED back to draft, start (guard), complete, cancel. Assignment cancellation
9. Crew profile: mc profile show, skills, availability
10. Scripted end-to-end CLI demo + test results in README

### P1: Next extensions: If time permits in this session
#### Crew and skills
1. Directors manage org settings
    - Skill catalogue
#### Mission lifecyle
2. Mission audit logs
#### Matching
3. Decision insights for lead: Excluded members: Why?
4. Rank breakdown per suggestion: Why is this the best person for the slot
#### CLI
5. Short references for missions (`MSN-<n>`) and skills (`slug`), see Short references
...

### P2: Scoped as outside of this session
#### Auth and tenant
1. Noisy-neighbour protection / uneven org sizes in this multi tenant architecture
2. Real idp oidc, login / signup, 
3. Postgres RLS as second layer for reads (composite FKs only protect writes / links)
4. User and role management
#### Mission lifecycle
5. Approval workflow customization
6. Crew members withdraw after accepting
7. Reject with comment, cancel with reason
8. Reassign the lead of a mission
#### Crew and skills
9. Edit / archive skills
10. Verification of self assessed proficiency
#### Matching
11. Additional resource constraints, extending the matching engine
12. No matches and report gap and potential resolutions
13. Rest buffer between missions
14. Mission priority
15. Optimize for larger orgs with lots of staff
#### Operations
16. CI / CD
17. Scalability, Observability, IaC, offline jobs, etc. 

## Ambiguity resolution
1. Different skill taxonomy per org -> Skills owned by each org with fixed proficiency scale (1-5). Skill names are unique per org: UNIQUE(org_id, name)
2. Different approval processes per org -> Initial scope will be one single director approval in code. Later extension to DB stored approval configs
3. Leads cannot approve their own missions -> One role per user with hierarchy Director > Lead, so a director can also lead missions. The mission lead can never approve their own mission. A director who is also leading a mission needs a second director to get approval. On mission creation the API and CLI flag that this mission requires an additional director for approval.
4. Who can be assinged to a mission: Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead is never a crew member and a director is never a crew member. The Director > Lead hierarchy does not include Crew.
5. Directors approve missions -> A mission to approve consists of requirements, timeline and date. Lead can preview the matcher in draft to check the mission can be staffed before submit. The director sees the same matcher preview in the approval view. Invites happen only after approval, so scarce skills are not reserved for unfunded missions. No separate steps for now
6. Changing after approval -> Missions can only be edited in draft. Before changing mission details after a director approved lead needs to withdraw the mission back to draft status. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments are then CANCELLED. Staffing changes (e.g. replacing a declined crew member) are not a change and need no new approval.
7. Availability tracking -> Instead of managing available periods it is more pragmatic to manage unavailable timeslots: holiday leave, sick leave, internal meetings, etc. Dates only. A crew member is blocked by unavailability, invited and accepted assignments.

from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from mc_api.dependencies import get_current_user, get_scope
from mc_api.errors import Forbidden
from mc_api.models import AppUser
from mc_api.scope import OrgScope
from mc_shared import UserOut, UserRole

router = APIRouter(prefix="/users", tags=["users"])


@router.get("/{user_id}")
def get_user(
    user_id: UUID,
    user: Annotated[AppUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
    scope: Annotated[OrgScope, Depends(get_scope)],
) -> UserOut:
    # The scope lookup runs first, so another org gives 404 before any role check.
    target = scope.get(AppUser, user_id)
    if user.role == UserRole.CREW and target.id != user.id:
        raise Forbidden(UserRole.CREW, "Crew members view only their own profile")
    return UserOut(
        id=target.id,
        username=target.username,
        display_name=target.display_name,
        role=target.role,
    )

def get_user(
    user_id: UUID,
    user: Annotated[AppUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
    scope: Annotated[OrgScope, Depends(get_scope)],
) -> UserOut:
    # The scope lookup runs first, so another org gives 404 before any role check.

        id=target.id,
        username=target.username,
        display_name=target.display_name,
        role=target.role,
    )

The reference window for the matcher is 2027-01-11 to 2027-01-24 in org Artemis Space Agency.
The DRAFT mission "Polar Ice Survey" uses this window.

Run the matcher preview as its lead:
```sh
uv run mc login --user leo
uv run mc missions list
uv run mc missions match <id of "Polar Ice Survey">
```

## Configuration
The defaults match `docker-compose.yml`, so the run steps need no configuration. To override a value, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, edit it and load it with `uv run --env-file .env <command>`.

| Variable | Default | Used by |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql+psycopg://mc:mc@localhost:5432/mc` | API, Alembic |
| `JWT_SECRET` | `dev-only-secret-change-me-0123456789` | API |
| `MC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` | CLI |
| `MC_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.config/mc` | CLI |

@router.get("/{mission_id}/match")
def match_preview(
    mission_id: UUID,
    scope: Scope,
    user: Annotated[AppUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
) -> MatchPreview:
    mission = scope.get(Mission, mission_id)
    if mission.lead_id != user.id:
        raise Forbidden(user.role, "Directors and leads run the matcher only on their own missions")
    if mission.status != MissionStatus.DRAFT:
        logger.info("match preview rejected: mission %s is %s", mission.id, mission.status)
        raise HTTPException(
            409, f"Mission is {mission.status}. The matcher preview is allowed only in DRAFT."
        )
    slots = mission_out(scope, mission).slots
    rows = scope.session.execute(
        scope.select(CrewSkill)
        .add_columns(AppUser)
        .join(AppUser, (AppUser.org_id == CrewSkill.org_id) & (AppUser.id == CrewSkill.user_id))
        .where(AppUser.role == UserRole.CREW)
    ).all()
    users: dict[UUID, AppUser] = {}
    skills: dict[UUID, dict[UUID, int]] = {}
    holders: dict[UUID, int] = {}
    for cs, u in rows:
        users[u.id] = u
        skills.setdefault(u.id, {})[cs.skill_id] = cs.level
        holders[cs.skill_id] = holders.get(cs.skill_id, 0) + 1

    busy = set(
        scope.session.scalars(
            scope.select(Unavailability)
            .where(overlaps(Unavailability, mission))
            .with_only_columns(Unavailability.user_id)
        )
    )
    busy |= set(
        scope.session.scalars(
            scope.select(Assignment)
            .where(
                Assignment.mission_id == mission.id,
                Assignment.status == AssignmentStatus.DECLINED,
            )

def editable_mission(scope: OrgScope, user: AppUser, mission_id: UUID) -> Mission:
    """Lock the mission of the lead. 404, then 403 for a non-owner, then 409 if not DRAFT."""
    mission = scope.get(Mission, mission_id, for_update=True)
    if mission.lead_id != user.id:
        raise Forbidden(user.role, "Directors and leads edit only their own missions")

        raise HTTPException(409, f"Mission is {mission.status}. Edits are allowed only in DRAFT.")
    return mission

# Spec: mission-approval

## Goal
Add the mission approval of build step 6 (`design/DESIGN.md:69`) to the API and the CLI. The lead submits and withdraws a mission. A director who does not lead the mission approves or rejects it, and sees the matcher preview in the mission view (DESIGN req 8, 9).

## Acceptance criteria

@app.command()
def match(mission_id: str) -> None:
    """Show the closest-fit crew member for each slot of a DRAFT mission that you lead."""
    path = f"/missions/{quote(mission_id, safe='')}/match"
    preview = MatchPreview.model_validate(request("GET", path).json())
    table = Table("Slot", "Skill", "Min level", "Crew", "Level", "Workload days")
    for m in preview.slots:
        s, c = m.slot, m.suggestion
        table.add_row(
            str(s.position),
            s.skill_name,
            str(s.min_level),
            c.username if c else "No match",
            str(c.level) if c else "",
            str(c.workload_days) if c else "",
        )
    console.print(table)
    filled = sum(m.suggestion is not None for m in preview.slots)
    console.print(f"{filled} of {len(preview.slots)} slots filled")

@router.get("/{mission_id}")
def get_mission(mission_id: UUID, scope: Scope) -> MissionOut:
    return mission_out(scope, scope.get(Mission, mission_id))


def editable_mission(scope: OrgScope, user: AppUser, mission_id: UUID) -> Mission:
    """Lock the mission of the lead. 404, then 403 for a non-owner, then 409 if not DRAFT."""
    mission = scope.get(Mission, mission_id, for_update=True)
    if mission.lead_id != user.id:
        raise Forbidden(user.role, "Directors and leads edit only their own missions")
    if mission.status != MissionStatus.DRAFT:
        logger.info("edit of mission %s rejected: status %s", mission.id, mission.status)
        raise HTTPException(409, f"Mission is {mission.status}. Edits are allowed only in DRAFT.")
    return mission

    path = f"/missions/{quote(mission_id, safe='')}/match"
    preview = MatchPreview.model_validate(request("GET", path).json())
    table = Table("Slot", "Skill", "Min level", "Crew", "Level", "Workload days")
    for m in preview.slots:

        table.add_row(

            s.skill_name,
            str(s.min_level),
            c.username if c else "No match",

## Goal
Add the org crew view of build step 10 (`design/DESIGN.md:73`) to the API and the CLI. Directors and leads list the crew members of their org and show one crew member with skills, leave and current assignments (requirement 11, `design/DESIGN.md:35`). Leads see leave without the reason (`design/DESIGN.md:184`, `design/DESIGN.md:332`).

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Only directors and leads use the crew routes (DESIGN 332, 334). | A crew member gets 403 on `GET /crew` and on `GET /crew/{user_id}`. The body is `{"role": "CREW", "rule": "Only directors and leads view the org crew"}`. A request without a token gets 401. |
| AC2 | A director and a lead list the crew members of the org (DESIGN req 11). | `GET /crew` gives 200 and one item `{"id", "username", "display_name"}` for each user with the role `CREW` in the own org, sorted by username. It has no director, no lead and no user of another org. |
| AC3 | The list filters by username. | `GET /crew?username=<u>` gives 200 and exactly one item for a crew member of the own org. It gives `[]` for an unknown username, for a director or lead, and for a crew member of another org. The match is exact. |
| AC4 | A director and a lead show one crew member (DESIGN req 11). | `GET /crew/{user_id}` gives 200 and `{"id", "username", "display_name", "skills", "unavailability", "assignments"}`. `skills` has one item `{"skill_id", "skill_name", "level"}` for each skill of the crew member, sorted by skill name. |
| AC5 | The view shows all leave of the crew member. | `unavailability` has one item `{"start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` for each entry of the crew member, past and future, sorted by `start_date`, then `end_date`. It has no entry of another user. |
| AC6 | A director sees the leave reason. A lead does not (DESIGN 184, 332). | For a director, `reason` is the stored value, for example `"SICK"`. For a lead, `reason` is `null` on each entry. The lead gets the same entries and dates as the director. |
| AC7 | The view shows the current commitments of the crew member. | `assignments` has one item `{"mission_id", "mission_title", "mission_status", "start_date", "end_date", "slot_position", "skill_name", "status"}` for each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment on a mission that is not COMPLETED or CANCELLED, sorted by mission start date, then slot position. A DECLINED or CANCELLED assignment is not in the list. An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission is not in the list. |
| AC8 | Only crew members of the own org are visible (DESIGN req 4, 22, 381). | `GET /crew/{user_id}` gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}` for a random UUID, for a user of another org, and for a director or lead of the own org. The three bodies are the same. A bad UUID gives 422. |
| AC9 | The CLI lists the crew (DESIGN req 11). | `mc crew list` calls `GET /crew` and shows a table with the columns `Username` and `Name`. A 401 or 403 exits 1 with the API message and no traceback. |
| AC10 | The CLI shows one crew member by username (DESIGN 442). | `mc crew show <username>` calls `GET /crew?username=<username>`, then `GET /crew/{id}`. It shows the username, the display name, a skills table, an unavailability table and an assignments table. A `null` reason shows as `unavailable`. An unknown username, or a username of another org, exits 1 with `Not found` and no traceback. A 403 exits 1 with the role and the rule. |

## Non-goals
- A change of `GET /users/{user_id}`. It stays as it is for all roles.
- A view of directors and leads in the crew view.
- A date filter on the unavailability. The view shows all entries, like `mc profile availability list`.
- Assignment history (DECLINED, CANCELLED, finished missions) in the crew view.
- Workload days in the crew view. The matcher preview shows them.
- The unavailability `id` in the crew view. Only the crew member removes an entry.
- Skills in the `mc crew list` table.
- Case-insensitive usernames. The change log puts them in P2 (commit `699f416`).
- A schema change or a migration. The tables of step 2 have all the columns.

+## Demo
+`scripts/demo.sh` runs the full mission journey with the `mc` CLI. It shows one heading line for each step, then each `mc` command with its output.
+
+Prerequisites: Postgres runs (`docker compose up -d`). The API runs (`uv run uvicorn mc_api.main:app`).
+
+**Warning:** The script deletes all data in the database of `DATABASE_URL`. Step 1 runs `mc-seed`. Use it only on a local demo database.
+
+```sh
+bash scripts/demo.sh
+```
+
+The script uses a temporary folder for the token, so it does not replace your token. Set `MC_CONFIG_DIR` to change this. The script also reads `MC_API_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. It sets `COLUMNS=200` so tables do not wrap.
+
+| Step | Title |
+|------|-------|
+| 1 | Reset the demo data |
+| 2 | Crew profile (`ben`): show the profile, set a skill, add and remove leave |
+| 3 | Create the mission and its slots (`leo`) |
+| 4 | Matcher preview in DRAFT (`leo`) |
+| 5 | Submit (`leo`) and approve (`diana`) |
+| 6 | Invite, accept and decline: `ben` accepts, `hana` declines |
+
+## Known gaps
+The demo does not show these items:
+- Rematch of open slots after a decline (requirement 19).
+- The 403 and 404 checks. The tests cover them.
+- Start, complete and cancel of a mission (build step 8).
+- The org-wide crew view and mission view for directors (build step 10, requirement 11).
+
 ## Configuration
 The defaults match `docker-compose.yml`, so the run steps need no configuration. To override a value, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, edit it and load it with `uv run --env-file .env <command>`.
 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo of the full mission journey. Warning: step 1 deletes all data (mc-seed).
# Needs Postgres and the API running. Reads MC_API_URL, MC_CONFIG_DIR, DATABASE_URL, COLUMNS.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
export COLUMNS="${COLUMNS:-200}"
if [ -z "${MC_CONFIG_DIR:-}" ]; then
  MC_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$MC_CONFIG_DIR"' EXIT
  export MC_CONFIG_DIR
fi

OUT=""
heading() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$1"; }
# Print the command, run it, and keep its output in $OUT for the next steps.
mc() {
  local a shown=""
  for a in "$@"; do [[ $a == *" "* ]] && a="\"$a\""; shown+=" $a"; done
  printf '$ mc%s\n' "$shown"
  OUT=$(uv run mc "$@")
  printf '%s\n' "$OUT"
}
# Print the first table cell (the ID) of the row that has the given name.
row_id() { awk -F'│' -v n="$1" '$3 ~ n {gsub(/ /, "", $2); print $2}' <<<"$OUT"; }

heading "1. Reset the demo data"
echo '$ mc-seed'
uv run mc-seed

heading "2. Crew profile (ben)"
mc login --user ben
mc profile show
mc skills list
geology=$(row_id Geology)
mc profile skills set "$geology" --level 3
mc profile skills list
mc profile availability add --from 2027-06-01 --to 2027-06-03 --reason HOLIDAY
leave=$(awk '/^Added unavailability/ {print $3}' <<<"$OUT")
mc profile availability list
mc profile availability remove "$leave"
mc profile availability list

heading "3. Create the mission and its slots (leo)"
mc login --user leo
mc skills list
piloting=$(row_id Piloting)
medicine=$(row_id Medicine)
mc missions create --title "Demo Survey" --start 2027-03-01 --end 2027-03-10
mission=$(awk '/^Created mission/ {print $3}' <<<"$OUT")
mc missions slots add "$mission" --skill "$piloting" --level 3
mc missions slots add "$mission" --skill "$medicine" --level 3

heading "4. Matcher preview in DRAFT (leo)"
mc missions match "$mission"

heading "5. Submit (leo) and approve (diana)"
mc missions submit "$mission"
mc login --user diana
mc missions approve "$mission"
